title: Bali Private Tours: A Better Way to Explore the Island
content:
Bali is an island of temples, rice terraces, waterfalls, beaches, villages and landscapes that can feel completely different from one day to the next. The challenge is knowing where to go, how to plan your time and how to experience more without spending your holiday rushing between places.
A private Bali tour gives you the flexibility to explore the island at your own pace, with an itinerary built around the places and experiences that interest you most.
Whether you want to discover the cultural side of Ubud, watch the sunset around Uluwatu, explore the dramatic landscapes of Nusa Penida or venture into the quieter parts of North Bali, a well-planned private tour can make your time on the island much easier and more rewarding.
Why Choose a Private Tour in Bali?
One of the biggest advantages of a private Bali tour is flexibility.
Instead of following a fixed group itinerary, you can plan your day around your interests, preferred pace and available time. You can spend longer at a place you enjoy, change the order of your stops and combine several experiences into one carefully planned day.
Private tours are particularly useful for travelers who want to see several parts of Bali during a short stay.
For example, a single day could combine cultural attractions, scenic landscapes and local experiences around Ubud. Another itinerary could focus on the southern coast, including Uluwatu and some of Bali's most impressive sunset locations.
The experience should fit your trip — not the other way around.
Ubud Private Tours
Ubud is one of the best places to experience the cultural and natural side of Bali.
The area is surrounded by rice terraces, temples, traditional villages, waterfalls and forest landscapes. A private Ubud tour allows you to combine several of these experiences without having to follow a rigid schedule.
Popular experiences around Ubud include:
Sacred Monkey Forest
Tegalalang Rice Terrace
Tirta Empul Temple
Traditional Balinese villages
Waterfalls
Local art and cultural experiences
Scenic countryside
Ubud is also a convenient starting point for exploring several areas of central Bali, making it a natural base for a private Bali day tour.
Uluwatu and South Bali Experiences
The southern part of Bali offers a very different atmosphere from Ubud.
Uluwatu is known for its dramatic cliffs, ocean views, beaches and spectacular sunsets. A private Uluwatu tour can combine several coastal locations into one relaxed day.
Depending on your itinerary, you can explore beaches, visit Uluwatu Temple, enjoy the coastline and finish the day watching the sunset over the Indian Ocean.
For travelers staying in areas such as Canggu, Seminyak, Legian, Kuta or Jimbaran, South Bali can be an excellent choice for a dedicated day of exploring.
Nusa Penida Day Tours
Nusa Penida is one of Bali's most recognizable island destinations, known for its dramatic cliffs, turquoise water and striking coastal scenery.
A Nusa Penida day tour can be planned around the areas you most want to see, including famous viewpoints and beaches.
Because travel times can vary significantly, planning the route properly is important. A well-organized itinerary helps you make better use of your time and avoid spending the entire day moving between locations.
For travelers with limited time in Bali, Nusa Penida can be an excellent addition to a wider Bali itinerary.
Exploring North Bali
North Bali offers a quieter side of the island and is ideal for travelers looking beyond the most visited areas.
The region is known for mountain scenery, waterfalls, lakes, temples and expansive landscapes.
A North Bali tour can include destinations such as Ulun Danu Beratan, Banyumala Waterfall, Leke Leke Waterfall and the Jatiluwih rice terraces.
The journey from the main tourist areas can take time, but the landscapes and slower pace make North Bali worthwhile for travelers looking for a different perspective of the island.
How to Choose the Right Bali Tour
The best Bali tour depends on where you are staying, how many days you have and what you want to experience.
If you are interested in culture, temples and countryside, consider an Ubud private tour.
If you prefer dramatic coastal scenery and sunsets, explore Uluwatu and South Bali.
If you want spectacular island landscapes, consider a Nusa Penida tour.
If you have more time and want to see a quieter side of the island, North Bali offers waterfalls, mountains, temples and scenic countryside.
You do not need to see everything in one day. Choosing the right combination of places usually creates a better experience than trying to visit every famous attraction.
Plan Your Bali Experience With Balance Island
At Balance Island, we believe exploring Bali should feel personal rather than rushed.
Our private Bali tours and experiences are designed around the places you want to see and the way you want to spend your time on the island.
From Ubud and its cultural landscapes to Uluwatu's dramatic coastline, Nusa Penida's natural scenery and the quieter destinations of North Bali, our collection of experiences makes it easier to discover different sides of Bali.
Explore our private Bali tours and find an experience that fits your journey.

title: How to Plan a Bali Itinerary: A Practical Guide to Exploring the Island
content: Planning a Bali trip can look simple on a map. The island is not particularly large, yet the experience of travelling between different regions can be very different from what you expect. Ubud, Uluwatu, Canggu, Nusa Penida and North Bali each offer something different. Trying to visit too many places in a single day can quickly turn a holiday into a schedule of traffic, transfers and rushed stops. A good Bali itinerary is not about seeing everything. It is about choosing the right places and giving yourself enough time to enjoy them. How Many Days Do You Need in Bali? For a first trip, seven to ten days gives you enough time to experience several sides of Bali without constantly changing locations. A shorter trip can still work well if you focus on one or two areas. For example: 3–4 days: Focus on Ubud and South Bali. 5–7 days: Add another region such as North Bali or Nusa Penida. 8–10 days: Combine several regions with more time for beaches, cultural experiences and slower days. The important thing is to avoid planning destinations based only on how close they appear on a map. Ubud: Culture, Rice Terraces and Central Bali Ubud is one of the best places to include in a Bali itinerary for travelers interested in culture and nature. You can explore temples, rice terraces, waterfalls, traditional villages and the surrounding countryside. A day around Ubud might include: Tegalalang Rice Terrace Tirta Empul Temple Sacred Monkey Forest Traditional Balinese villages Waterfalls Local cultural experiences Rather than trying to visit every attraction, choose several that fit naturally together. Uluwatu and South Bali South Bali offers a completely different experience. Uluwatu is known for dramatic cliffs, ocean views, beaches and sunsets. It works particularly well as a day or afternoon-to-evening experience. A South Bali itinerary can include coastal viewpoints, beaches, Uluwatu Temple and a sunset experience. If you are staying around Canggu, Seminyak, Kuta or Jimbaran, planning your southern destinations together can help reduce unnecessary travel. Should You Visit Nusa Penida? Nusa Penida is worth considering if dramatic coastal scenery is high on your list. The island is known for its cliffs, beaches and turquoise water, but it also requires careful planning because travel between locations can take longer than expected. If you only have one day, choose your route carefully instead of trying to cover every famous viewpoint. Don't Forget North Bali North Bali is often overlooked by first-time visitors. The region offers mountain scenery, waterfalls, lakes, temples and rice terraces, including destinations such as Ulun Danu Beratan, Banyumala and Jatiluwih. It takes longer to reach from many of Bali's main tourist areas, but that is part of the appeal. North Bali can feel noticeably quieter and less crowded. Build Your Bali Trip Around Experiences The strongest Bali itineraries are usually built around experiences rather than simply collecting destinations. Instead of asking: "How many places can I visit?" ask: "What do I actually want to experience?" That might be Balinese culture, dramatic landscapes, beaches, waterfalls, temples, food, photography or simply having a relaxed day exploring the countryside. Once you know what matters to you, the itinerary becomes much easier to build. Explore Bali With Balance Island Balance Island offers private Bali tours and carefully planned experiences designed around different parts of the island. Whether your trip takes you through Ubud, Uluwatu, North Bali, Nusa Penida or other destinations, choosing the right combination of places can make your time in Bali much more enjoyable. Explore the available Bali tours and experiences and build your trip around the parts of the island you genuinely want to discover.

title: 25 Best Things to Do in Ubud, Bali: The Complete 2026 Guide
content: Planning a trip to Ubud? From lush rice terraces and ancient temples to waterfalls, Balinese cooking classes, yoga, art and unforgettable local experiences, Ubud offers much more than a quick stop in Bali. Whether you're visiting Ubud for one day or spending a week exploring central Bali, this guide covers the best things to do, how to plan your time, and which experiences are worth prioritizing. What Is Ubud Known For? Ubud is best known as the cultural and wellness heart of Bali. It combines traditional Balinese culture with jungle landscapes, rice fields, temples, art galleries, restaurants and wellness experiences. Unlike Bali's beach destinations, Ubud is more about culture, nature, food, wellness and experiences. 1. Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest The Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary is one of Ubud's most recognizable attractions. The forest contains ancient temple complexes surrounded by dense tropical vegetation, with hundreds of long-tailed macaques living in the area. Why visit: Ancient temples Tropical forest Wildlife Beautiful photography opportunities Easy to combine with central Ubud Tip: Keep your belongings secure and don't intentionally feed or provoke the monkeys. 2. Walk the Campuhan Ridge For one of the easiest ways to experience Ubud's countryside, take a walk along Campuhan Ridge. The trail passes through green hills and valleys and provides a peaceful break from the busy streets of central Ubud. Best time to go: Early morning or late afternoon, when temperatures are cooler. Allow roughly 1–2 hours depending on how far you walk and how often you stop for photos. 3. Explore the Tegallalang Rice Terraces Tegallalang is famous for its dramatic rice terraces and is one of the most popular places to visit near Ubud. The landscape is particularly beautiful in the morning, when the light is softer and the surrounding countryside is cooler. You can walk around the terraces, visit nearby cafés and combine the area with other attractions in northern Ubud. Good for: Photography, couples, nature lovers and first-time visitors to Bali. 4. Visit Ubud Palace Located in the center of town, Ubud Palace is an easy attraction to add to your itinerary. The palace provides an introduction to Balinese architecture and royal history and is also associated with traditional Balinese dance performances. Because of its central location, it's easy to combine with Ubud Market and other attractions in downtown Ubud. 5. Browse Ubud Art Market If you're looking for souvenirs, handicrafts or traditional Balinese products, spend some time exploring Ubud Art Market. You'll find items such as: Handwoven products Clothing Artwork Bags Jewelry Decorative items Souvenirs Don't be afraid to compare prices and negotiate politely where appropriate. 6. Discover Balinese Art Ubud has a long association with Balinese painting, sculpture and traditional arts. Art lovers can visit museums and galleries around town to learn more about Balinese artistic traditions. If you're interested in art, don't limit yourself to the most famous attractions. Exploring smaller galleries can be one of the more rewarding ways to experience Ubud. 7. Visit a Balinese Temple Ubud and the surrounding villages are home to numerous temples. A temple visit is an opportunity to experience Balinese Hindu culture, architecture and daily religious traditions. Remember that temples are places of worship. Dress respectfully, follow local rules and check whether visitors are permitted to enter particular areas. 8. Watch a Traditional Balinese Dance A Balinese dance performance is one of the best cultural experiences to add to an evening in Ubud. Performances commonly combine music, elaborate costumes, storytelling and traditional choreography. Check the performance schedule before you go because shows take place at different venues and times. 9. Visit Tegenungan Waterfall Tegenungan Waterfall is one of the most accessible waterfalls from Ubud. The waterfall is surrounded by tropical greenery and viewing areas, with stairs leading toward the waterfall. It's a popular choice if you want to combine an Ubud trip with a short nature adventure. Tip: Visit earlier in the day if you want a quieter experience. 10. See Kanto Lampo Waterfall Kanto Lampo is another popular waterfall near Ubud. Unlike a traditional tall waterfall, water flows over a series of large rocks, creating a distinctive landscape. It can be combined with other attractions around southern and eastern Ubud. 11. Take a Balinese Cooking Class Food is one of the best ways to experience Balinese culture. A typical cooking class may include a visit to a local market followed by an introduction to ingredients, spices and traditional cooking techniques. You may learn to prepare dishes such as: Base genep spice paste Satay Lawar Traditional vegetable dishes Balinese sambal Cooking classes are especially good for travelers who want an experience rather than simply another sightseeing stop. 12. Try a Balinese Massage After a day exploring Ubud, a traditional Balinese massage can be a relaxing way to finish the day. Ubud has everything from simple local spas to high-end wellness resorts. If you're choosing a spa, compare the treatment menu, reviews and location before booking. 13. Join a Yoga Class Ubud has become internationally known for yoga and wellness. You'll find studios offering different styles and levels, from beginner-friendly classes to more advanced practices. Morning classes are a particularly good option if you want to start your sightseeing day feeling refreshed. 14. Try a Sound Healing or Wellness Experience Beyond yoga and massage, Ubud offers a wide range of wellness experiences. Depending on what's available during your visit, you may find: Sound healing Meditation Breathwork Spa treatments Wellness retreats Traditional healing experiences If you're new to wellness activities, look for beginner-friendly sessions with clear information about what the experience involves. 15. Go White-Water Rafting on the Ayung River For something more adventurous, consider rafting on the Ayung River. The activity combines river scenery, jungle landscapes and an outdoor adventure. Rafting trips typically include safety equipment and a guide, but check the operator's requirements before booking. 16. Explore Ubud by Bicycle Cycling is another way to see the countryside around Ubud. Rather than staying only in the town center, consider a guided cycling tour through villages, rice fields and rural areas. A guided tour can also give you more insight into local agriculture and everyday Balinese life. 17. Take an ATV Adventure If you're looking for something more adrenaline-filled, ATV tours are available around Ubud. Depending on the route, rides can pass through rural landscapes, dirt tracks, rice fields and villages. Choose an operator carefully and check what is included in the tour price, including safety equipment, transfers and insurance. 18. Visit Goa Gajah Goa Gajah, often called the Elephant Cave, is an archaeological and religious site near Ubud. The entrance features distinctive stone carvings, while the surrounding complex contains ancient structures, bathing pools and gardens. It's a worthwhile stop for travelers interested in Bali's history and spiritual heritage. 19. Visit Tirta Empul Temple Tirta Empul is one of Bali's best-known water temples. The temple is famous for its sacred spring water and purification ritual. Visitors should understand the difference between observing the ritual and participating in it. If you want to participate, follow the temple's rules and local guidance. 20. Explore the Ubud Countryside One of the best things to do in Ubud isn't a single attraction. Simply getting outside the town center can reveal a completely different side of Bali. Look for small roads through rice fields, traditional villages, local temples and family-run cafés. For many travelers, these quieter areas become some of their favorite memories of Ubud. 21. Eat Local Balinese Food Don't leave Ubud without trying local Indonesian and Balinese food. Look for dishes such as: Nasi campur — Rice served with a selection of vegetables, meat and other side dishes. Babi guling — Balinese-style roasted pork. Ayam betutu — Chicken cooked with a rich blend of spices. Lawar — A traditional Balinese mixed vegetable dish that can include meat or other ingredients. Sate — Grilled skewers served with various sauces and seasonings. Ubud also has an excellent selection of vegetarian and vegan restaurants, making it easy to find options for different diets. 22. Enjoy Ubud's Café Scene Ubud has a large café and restaurant scene, particularly around the central areas and popular neighborhoods. A good strategy is to combine sightseeing with café stops rather than trying to visit every attraction in a single day. Look for cafés with views over rice fields or jungle landscapes if you want something different from the busy town center. 23. Take a Day Trip From Ubud Ubud is also a convenient base for exploring other parts of Bali. Depending on your interests, possible day trips include: Mount Batur Kintamani Tirta Empul Sidemen Waterfalls around central Bali Traditional villages Northern Bali A private driver or organized tour can make it easier to visit multiple locations in one day. 24. Experience Ubud at Night Ubud isn't primarily a nightlife destination, but there is still plenty to do after sunset. Consider: Balinese dance performances Dinner at a local restaurant Night markets Live music Evening yoga or wellness sessions A relaxing spa treatment Ubud is generally better suited to a relaxed evening than a big party night. 25. Leave Time to Do Nothing This might be the most important Ubud recommendation. Don't fill every hour of your itinerary. Spend an afternoon sitting at a café, walking through the rice fields, getting a massage or simply enjoying your accommodation. Ubud is a destination where slowing down can be just as rewarding as sightseeing. Best Things to Do in Ubud for Different Travelers For first-time visitors Prioritize the Monkey Forest, Campuhan Ridge, Tegallalang Rice Terraces, Ubud Palace and a Balinese cultural experience. For couples Choose a combination of rice terraces, a spa treatment, a cooking class, a sunset experience and a nice dinner. For families Consider waterfalls, cultural attractions, cooking classes and carefully selected outdoor activities. For adventure travelers Try rafting, cycling, ATV tours, hiking and waterfall excursions. For wellness travelers Focus on yoga, massage, meditation, sound healing and healthy food. For culture lovers Visit temples, museums, art galleries, traditional performances and local villages. How Many Days Do You Need in Ubud? 1 day: Enough for a quick introduction, but you'll need to prioritize. 2–3 days: Ideal for seeing the major attractions while still having time to relax. 4–5 days: Better if you want to combine sightseeing with wellness, food and day trips. 1 week: Great for travelers who want to slow down and explore beyond the main tourist attractions. Suggested 3-Day Ubud Itinerary Day 1 — Ubud Culture Morning: Campuhan Ridge Walk Late morning: Ubud Palace Lunch: Local Balinese food Afternoon: Ubud Art Market and nearby galleries Evening: Traditional Balinese dance and dinner Day 2 — Rice Fields & Nature Morning: Tegallalang Rice Terraces Late morning: Local café or countryside exploration Afternoon: Waterfall visit Evening: Balinese massage Day 3 — Experience Bali Morning: Balinese cooking class Afternoon: Temple or village visit Late afternoon: Relax at your accommodation Evening: Dinner and a relaxed evening in Ubud What Is the Best Time to Visit Ubud? Ubud can be visited throughout the year. The dry season is generally popular with travelers because outdoor activities and sightseeing are easier to plan. The wet season can bring heavier rain, but it can also mean greener landscapes and fewer crowds at some attractions. Regardless of the season, plan outdoor activities for the morning when possible. How to Get Around Ubud Your best transportation option depends on where you're staying and what you want to see. For central Ubud, many attractions can be reached by walking. For attractions outside the center, common options include: Scooter Private driver Taxi Ride-hailing services Organized tours Cycling tours If you're not experienced riding a scooter, hiring a driver or using another transportation option is generally a more comfortable choice. Final Thoughts Ubud is one of the best places in Bali for travelers who want more than a beach holiday. The combination of Balinese culture, temples, rice terraces, waterfalls, food, art, wellness and outdoor adventures makes it easy to create a trip around your own interests. If you're visiting for the first time, don't try to see everything. Pick a few major attractions, add one or two local experiences, and leave some time to simply enjoy Ubud. And before booking an activity, check recent reviews, what's included, cancellation conditions and the exact meeting point. Planning your Ubud trip? Save this guide and use it as your starting point for building your itinerary.
